source.title: Dispersion Loss Counteracts Embedding Condensation and Improves Generalization in Small Language Models
source.authors: Chen Liu; Xing-Zhi Sun; Xi Xiao; Alexandre Van Tassel; Ke Xu; Kristof Reimann; Dan-Qi Liao; Mark Gerstein; Tian-Yang Wang; Xiao Wang; Smita Krishnaswamy

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies embedding geometry and dispersion-based training, not the claimed cross-entropy scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation. It cites scaling-law work as background but does not test or use those laws.
record.gate_note: The reported model-size comparisons measure embedding condensation, not held-out cross-entropy loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The dispersion-loss experiments measure geometry and benchmark performance under a training intervention; they do not test downstream predictability from model scale or pretraining loss. These related but different findings are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. only as background. It measures embedding-geometry condensation (Spearman/Kendall correlations of layer-wise cosine similarity) across model sizes, and benchmark gains from a dispersion regularizer. It reports no held-out loss scaling, power-law fits, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, fixed-parameter shape comparisons, or tests of downstream predictability from scale or loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased: smaller Transformers suffer more embedding condensation, distillation does not fix it, and a dispersion loss counteracts it and gives modest benchmark gains in small models.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies embedding geometry and a dispersion regularizer; it does not implement or evaluate the original scaling-law methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Embedding-condensation trends are reported as consistent across several model families and input-text datasets. The authors also report that dispersion loss is relatively robust to the tested weighting coefficient and temperature choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Within GPT2, Qwen1, Qwen2.5, Qwen3 and Bloom families, and in a controlled four-model GPT2-like MLP-width sweep, larger models show less layer-wise embedding condensation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embedding condensation decreases with model size within Transformer families.

fits_no_version.finding: Olmo-3-7B condensation correlations are strongly positive at initialization and become negative over pretraining. Distillation from DeepSeek-R1 does not transfer dispersion to Qwen2.5 students.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Condensation is an initialization effect counteracted by pretraining, and it is not removed by logit distillation.

fits_no_version.finding: A dispersion regularizer reduces condensation and raises the 10-benchmark average. In Qwen3-0.6B pretraining the average rises from 34.84 to 36.01.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dispersion-aware training improves small-model benchmark averages without extra parameters.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The paper does not test the claimed loss-scaling relationships. Several embedding-geometry comparisons are presented mainly in figures without numerical values in the text; the reported benchmark results concern dispersion-loss interventions rather than predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the scaling-law claim were applicable. Table 2 contains many separate mid-training benchmark entries for alternative training methods, but these are not measures of any listed claim version.

untested.parts: All: no loss-vs-parameters/tokens/compute sweeps or power-law fits.
All: no small-run fits extrapolated to larger runs.
All: no fixed-compute allocation of parameters and tokens.
All: the controlled MLP-width sweep varies parameter count and measures embedding geometry, not loss at fixed parameters.
All: no scaling-law form tested in other modalities or regimes.
All: base-model benchmark averages across sizes appear in Table 2 only as reference points. Predictability from scale or loss is not analysed.
All: no analysis of fitting choices or exponent variation.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 lists untrained base-model averages that rise with size (e.g. GPT2 34.35 to GPT2-xl around 40.89; Qwen3-0.6B 44.11 to 14B 65.93). These are incidental reference numbers, not a scaling analysis, so they are not treated as V6 evidence. The rows are correctly set to versions none.

versions.untested_parts: The full version: no power-law fits or held-out cross-entropy loss sweeps over parameters, tokens, or compute.
The full version: no small-run fits or predictions of larger-run loss.
The full version: no fixed-compute search or measurement of optimal parameter and token allocations.
The full version: no comparison of loss across architectural variations at fixed parameter count.
The full version: no tests of scaling-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
The full version: benchmark results under dispersion-loss training are not tests of downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
The full version: no analysis of scaling-law fit choices, exponent variation, or loss-curve bends.

rows.subject: GPT2, Qwen1, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, and Bloom model families (aggregate trend)
rows.size_stated: Multiple sizes within each family; individual sizes not stated here
rows.operation_detail: Compared embedding condensation across model sizes within families

conditions.value: Layer-wise pairwise embedding cosine-similarity trends, summarized with Spearman correlation and Kendall's Tau

rows.value: Within each family, larger models are less susceptible to embedding condensation.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative trend across model families; this is a representation-geometry result, not a loss-scaling measurement.

rows.subject: Four GPT2-like models (aggregate result; individual model names and sizes not stated)
rows.size_stated: Four sizes; only MLP dimension varies
rows.operation_detail: Pre-trained controlled model-size sweep varying MLP dimension while holding other listed factors fixed

conditions.value: Number of layers, embedding dimension, dataset, and training settings

rows.value: Larger models consistently exhibit less embedding condensation.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend for the four-model experiment but does not give numerical values in the text.

rows.subject: Olmo-3-1025-7B
rows.stage_stated: Initialization, intermediate pretraining stages, and final base model
rows.operation_detail: Tracked embedding-condensation measures across training checkpoints
rows.measure: Spearman and Kendall correlations summarizing layer depth versus embedding similarity
rows.value: Both correlation measures are strongly positive at initialization, decrease during training, and eventually become negative.
rows.note: The result concerns embedding geometry over training, not held-out cross-entropy loss.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 family distilled models and scratch-trained counterparts (aggregate result)
rows.size_stated: A range of model sizes; individual sizes not stated here
rows.stage_stated: Distilled models compared with models trained from scratch
rows.operation_detail: Compared embedding-condensation trends in distilled models and scratch-trained counterparts
rows.value: The trends closely mirror those of non-distilled models; distillation does not consistently alleviate condensation in smaller models or amplify dispersion in larger models.
rows.note: This is a qualitative result about distillation and embedding geometry.

rows.subject: Pre-trained GPT2
rows.operation_detail: Continued training with dispersion loss versus the standard cross-entropy objective
rows.baseline: Continued training with the standard cross-entropy objective
rows.value: Standard training provides minimal relief; dispersion-loss training substantially spreads out cosine-similarity distributions.
rows.note: The intervention and outcome concern embedding geometry rather than any scaling-law version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-0.6B
rows.operation_detail: Added dispersion loss to the training objective
